macro: US equity futures are in the red Thursday morning with the S&P down 44 points, Nasdaq off 105 basis points, and broad weakness across European and Asian markets. The big story is the lack of progress on US-Iran diplomacy, which is sending Brent crude spiking 275 basis points back to around $106 after briefly dipping below $100 just 36 hours ago. The Trump-Xi summit is expected to be long on pageantry and short on substance, with the Busan Agreement extended only two months — a deeply underwhelming outcome that markets are digesting negatively.
rates_fed: The 10- and 30-year Treasury yields are climbing 2 to 3 basis points, extending gains from Wednesday's blowout flash PMIs, while 2-year yields are flat. Markets are pricing in 38 basis points of additional Fed hikes this year with odds of an October 28th hike above 70%, plus another roughly 55 basis points in 2027. The Japanese yen continues to weaken back toward the 160 level versus the dollar, and Fed Governor Barr on Wednesday became the latest official to warn that further tightening will be needed.
market_outlook: Adam is leaning bearish for Thursday's session. The twin headwinds of rising oil prices due to stalled Iran diplomacy and climbing yields from hot PMI data are the dominant pressure points. The key catalyst to watch is the Trump-Xi White House meeting — but the base case is status quo, meaning no meaningful positive surprise, which leaves the market vulnerable to further selling.
bull_case: The White House is acutely aware that the yield problem is at crisis levels, which could force a refocus on Iran policy — the one lever the administration can pull most quickly to bring energy prices and yields back down. If the Trump-Xi summit produces even modest incremental goodwill or trade clarity, it could serve as a short-term relief catalyst. Darden Restaurants earnings before the open and Costco after the close could provide positive consumer read-throughs if results are strong.
bear_case: Oil is back at $106 and yields are still climbing — a toxic combination for equity valuations and consumer spending. The Iran diplomatic track appears to be stalling, and the US-China summit looks set to disappoint with only a two-month Busan extension rather than any structural deal. Flash PMIs confirmed both strong growth and very hot inflation with supply chain chaos, which only reinforces the Fed's hawkish posture and makes a rate cut cycle even more distant. AI news flow over the past week has been net negative in aggregate, adding pressure to mega-cap tech.

company_items.summary: Zuckerberg's Meta Connect keynote Wednesday night was at best inline with expectations. While AI narrative remains positively focused on Muse's momentum, the broader AI news flow from the industry over the past week has been net negative. The keynote did not deliver meaningful upside surprise.

Google is nearing the release of its next-generation flagship frontier model, Gemini 4, according to the head of its DeepMind unit. This is a significant product milestone in the escalating AI model race and signals Google is closing the gap with competitors.

Boeing is unlikely to receive an incremental plane order from China during the Trump-Xi summit this week. The company is instead focused on finalizing the 200-unit order announced back in May, and Reuters reports hope for a new deal has largely faded. This is a missed opportunity for a meaningful positive catalyst.

An FDA advisory committee recommended approval for Grail's multicancer blood test, though support was somewhat tepid regarding effectiveness and overall benefits. The outcome was largely expected following the earlier publication of briefing documents, limiting the upside surprise.

Knife River is facing activist pressure from Starboard Value, with the hedge fund pushing the construction company to consider a sale. This type of activist entry typically puts a floor under the stock and could attract strategic interest.

McDonald's shares slumped after the company's analyst meeting revealed Q3 comparable sales are tracking slightly below consensus. Free cash flow conversion will also fall short of prior guidance due to higher capital spending, though the company did provide a 2030 operating margin target that came in ahead of expectations.

Barry Diller on Wednesday withdrew People Inc's proposed takeout bid for MGM Resorts, removing a near-term acquisition premium from the stock. However, Diller said he remains open to and interested in a strategic transaction with the casino giant, keeping some optionality alive.

Paramount is looking to raise equity to bolster its balance sheet as the Warner deal moves closer to completion, and the company is reportedly considering tapping Elon Musk for an investment. Equity dilution risk is a near-term overhang even as the strategic combination with Warner advances.

HB Fuller reported modest upside on EPS and EBITDA — $1.52 and $187 million versus Street estimates of $1.46 and consensus — driven by margin expansion with gross margins up 120 basis points and EBITDA margins up 80 basis points as pricing increases offset raw material inflation. Sales were inline at $938 million and guidance was left approximately unchanged with the new EPS midpoint at roughly $4.77 versus the prior $4.75.

Eli Lilly struck a research collaboration and licensing agreement with China's InnoCare Pharma worth up to $3.35 billion. The deal expands Lilly's pipeline access and reinforces its aggressive push into new therapeutic areas.

sectors: Energy is the standout sector to watch — Brent back at $106 on stalled Iran diplomacy is bullish for energy stocks but a major headwind for the broader market via yields and inflation. AI and tech are under pressure as the Meta Connect keynote disappointed and broader AI news flow over the past week has been net negative; Raspberry Pi's CEO also noted memory prices are at or near their peak, which could weigh on semiconductor sentiment. European industrials, autos, tech, and banks are underperforming this morning. Nicotine and tobacco names could get a lift from reports that the FDA may ease restrictions and allow faster product launches.

tts_summary:
Good morning. Here is your morning game plan for Thursday, September 24th.

The macro picture is firmly risk-off. S&P futures are down 44 points, the Nasdaq is off over 100 basis points, and European markets are down 50 to 60 basis points with industrials, autos, and banks leading the losses. Asia was mostly lower overnight with Chinese mainland markets down nearly 2 percent.

The two big stories are the ones that are not happening. First, US-Iran diplomacy is stalling. Trump's comments Tuesday generated some optimism, but the rhetoric since then has been far less hopeful — and with no real progress toward a deal, Brent crude has spiked 275 basis points back to around $106 a barrel after briefly trading below $100 just 36 hours ago. That oil move is feeding directly into yields, with 10- and 30-year Treasuries climbing another 2 to 3 basis points on top of Wednesday's blowout flash PMI-driven gains. The market is now pricing in 38 basis points of additional Fed hikes this year, with odds of an October 28th hike above 70 percent, plus another 55 basis points in 2027. The dollar is firm and the yen is creeping back toward 160.

Second, the Trump-Xi summit at the White House looks set to disappoint. The best case is a two-month extension of the Busan Agreement — pushing the trade truce from November 10th to January 10th — which is underwhelming. Boeing is reportedly not going to get a new plane order from China this week. Expect pageantry and photo ops but not a market-moving positive surprise.

On the company side: Meta's Connect keynote from Zuckerberg Wednesday night landed as inline at best, and the broader AI news flow over the past week has been net negative for the sector. Google is nearing the launch of Gemini 4, its next flagship frontier model, which is a meaningful step in the AI arms race. McDonald's is under pressure after warning at an analyst meeting that third quarter comps are tracking slightly below consensus and that free cash flow conversion will disappoint. HB Fuller delivered a modest earnings beat driven by margin expansion. Grail got an FDA advisory committee recommendation for its multicancer blood test, though the support was tepid. Knife River has Starboard Value pushing for a sale — typically a floor-setter. And Eli Lilly announced a partnership with China's InnoCare worth up to 3.35 billion dollars, adding pipeline depth.

The directional lean today is bearish. Rising oil, rising yields, and a summit that won't deliver — that is a tough tape. The one silver lining is that the White House should be feeling serious pain from the yield surge, which may accelerate action on Iran. But for today, the pressure points are clear. Watch Darden before the open and Costco after the close for consumer read-throughs, and keep a close eye on any headlines out of the White House as Xi arrives around 10 AM Eastern. Stay disciplined.
